business_problem: KFC Australia's legacy SQL database could not keep up with rising data volumes, complex reporting requests, and partner-sharing needs, making analysis slow and limiting how quickly the business could act on operational and customer insight.
solution_summary: KFC Australia rebuilt its core analytical database on Snowflake after a single on-premises SQL database could no longer support the volume of operational, delivery, marketing, and supply-chain data needed for reporting. The initial proof of concept reran reports that had previously stalled for hours or days and returned them in 20 seconds, after which Snowflake became the shared platform for more than 2 million transaction records and over 10,000 extractions and reports each day. Instead of copying large datasets into Azure for franchisees and analysts, KFC now shares the same governed Snowflake data with suppliers, agencies, and other external partners, so everyone works from the latest sales and operational view without manual movement or duplication. The platform also centralizes data from the mobile app, website, and in-store point-of-sale terminals to build customer profiles and improve menu and service decisions while reducing database operating costs by 70%.
